newsitem.title: USA: California wheat, barley harvests underway.
newsitem.headline: California wheat, barley harvests underway.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the California Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ending August 3.

Field activities progressed normally under favorable conditions in most areas. Grain harvests of wheat and barley began in higher elevation fields. Small grain stubble was baled for straw or disced under in preparation for next year's crop. Rice was growing well in the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, and progress was nearly two weeks ahead of normal in most fields. Cotton was blooming and setting bolls in the San Joaquin and Sacramento valleys. Cotton growers were actively spraying for aphids, lygus, mites, whiteflies, worms and weeds. Harvest of corn for silage continued in central and southern counties. Seed alfalfa harvest was underway in the central and southern San Joaquin Valley. Blackeye beans were nearing maturity in southern counties. Some fields were treated for worms. Garbanzo beans, safflower and sugarbeets were harvested.
Alfalfa and sudangrass were cut for hay or greenchopped.

Almond harvest continued in the southern San Joaquin Valley and on the westside of Fresno County. The Fuji apple harvest began as the harvest of Gala apples continued. Prune sizes were generally smaller than last year. Table grape harvesting was still ahead of last year, with quality the highest in recent years. Raisin growers were preparing beds for drying. Peach, nectarine, plum and fig
harvests continued. Valencia orange picking continued. Citrus orchards were treated for scale, topped, hedged and irrigated.

Broccoli, cauliflower and lettuce were harvested in the coastal areas. Processing tomato harvest continued. Whitewash was sprayed on some processing tomatoes to prevent sunburn. Harvest of carrots in Kings and Kern counties continued. Potato harvest progressed in Kern County. Pumpkins were developing normally. Harvesting of

melons was increasing in the Sacramento Valley, while declining in the southern San Joaquin Valley. Sweet corn fields were treated to control worms. Bell peppers were sprayed to control whitefly, aphids and worms. Ground preparation for fall vegetables in Imperial County continued. Other crops harvested were: sweet corn, bell peppers, radishes, carrots, bell peppers, eggplant, squash, cucumbers, onions, okra, green beans and sweet potatoes.

Rangeland forage remained in good condition at higher elevations, and poor condition in the foothills. Stock water was adequate in most areas. Supplemental feeding was necessary at lower elevations. Livestock were in good condition.
